subject: AWS Marketplace private offer - term & approver checklist
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@procureco.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:02:00Z
Subject: AWS private offer - pricing/term questions for PO

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier. Procurement is ready to move to a Marketplace private offer but we have a few gating items before the CFO will sign:

- Term/Price mix: our CFO is pushing for a 12-month committed term; however they will consider a 3-month pilot if the invoice can be prorated and there's an opt-out at the 90-day mark. Can you confirm how Redwood invoices for partial periods (proration rules)?
- Approver roster: procurement needs a short list of the buyer-side approvers (finance, legal, security) so we can prepare internal reviews.
- Evidence pack: they require SOC 2 Type II evidence plus a short summary of data residency and key management integrations.
- Doc flow: prefer a signed PO + Marketplace private offer activation (we use DocuSign).

If you can share a proposed PO template and a short mutual action plan with milestones (legal review, finance approval, activation date) we can try to compress approvals.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, ProcureCo
maya.patel@procureco.com

Attachments: none
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@procureco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS private offer - pricing/term questions for PO

Hi Maya — really appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and an attached starter pack.

- Proration: Redwood invoices on a calendar-based cycle aligned to Marketplace activation. For private offers we can set the billing start date to the first of the next month or the activation date and prorate the first invoice to the day based on total committed amount. Example: activate Nov 20, invoice covers Nov 20–Dec 31 at pro-rated amount, then normal monthly/quarterly billing after. We can include explicit proration language in the PO.

- Term options we commonly offer:
  * 12-month commitment — standard discounted rate (baseline price).
  * 3-month pilot — 10% premium on unit price, but with an explicit 90-day exit clause. Good for fast approval cycles.
  * 6-month staged — splits commitment into pilot + conversion with pre-agreed conversion rates.

- Approver roster: please share the names/emails for the CFO and procurement lead. From our side, I'll include Finance (Laura) and Sales Ops (Vanessa) on the approval path.

- Evidence pack: attached (evidence-pack.pdf) — includes SOC 2 summary, network diagram, KMS integrations, and a 1-page data residency statement. If ProcureCo needs the full report we can route the NDA/data-room link.

I attached a draft PO template (draft-private-offer-PO.pdf) with placeholders for billing cadence and proration rules and a proposed MAP:

Mutual action plan (proposed)
1) 11/26 — Share PO template + evidence pack (done)
2) 11/27–11/30 — Procurement & legal review (ProcureCo)
3) 12/01 — Redwood legal review of any redlines
4) 12/03 — Sign PO + submit AWS private offer
5) 12/05 — Marketplace activation target (billing start date configurable)

If you prefer the 3-month pilot, I can mark the PO accordingly and propose a 10% premium and the 90-day opt-out clause. Let me know who I should send the DocuSign envelope to.

Best,
Elliot Price
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: evidence-pack.pdf, draft-private-offer-PO.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T13:07:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS private offer - pricing/term questions for PO

Elliot — quick finance checklist to speed internal approval. Copying Vanessa for sales-side policy sign-off.

1) PO vs Marketplace timing: finance needs a signed PO with the marketplace private offer ID referenced to accept proration. The activation billing date must be explicit. If ProcureCo wants a mid-month activation, we will include a pro-rated first invoice — confirm exact activation day in the PO.

2) Invoice schedule and payment terms: standard is Net 30 from invoice date. If the CFO needs Net 45/60, we need an internal credit exception and legal approval.

3) Evidence & contractual redlines: attach the redlines.docx with any changes they mark up — we need to surface any commercial changes vs. Marketplace standard terms (termination, liability, indemnity). Small operational redlines are fine; anything that expands indemnity or changes data residency triggers legal escalations.

4) CFO signoff delegation: if ProcureCo's CFO will not sign, a delegated finance approver with authority (email or documented signoff) is acceptable. Please confirm approver name + title.

I will prepare a filled draft-private-offer-PO.pdf with the billing clause and proration language once Elliot confirms the activation date and buyer approver list. If ProcureCo pushes for a 90-day pilot with proration, finance is generally OK if the pilot price has a modest premium (we usually accept up to 15% premium for pilots).

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: redlines.docx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:34:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS private offer - pricing/term questions for PO

Quick decision: approve a short 3-month pilot concession to accelerate close. Guidance below — follow through ASAP.

- Pilot pricing: offer +10% on list for 3 months, include explicit 90-day opt-out. If procurement wants the 12-month commitment, hold pricing at baseline and require finance escalation for any extended payment terms.
- Billing/overage: add a capped overage clause (first 3 months capped at 125% usage of committed amount) to reduce CFO concerns.
- Legal/Redlines: push back on any indemnity expansions. If ProcureCo asks to move data residency obligations, escalate to Legal.
- DocuSign flow: send DocuSign to Maya + ProcureCo legal and cc our finance (laura) and sales ops (me).

Elliot — fill the PO with activation date = 2026-12-05 (as proposed), set first invoice to be pro-rated Nov 20–Dec 4 if activation earlier, and queue the DocuSign. If they need a two-week close, I'm available to jump on a call with their CFO.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
